chunks: Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad al-Sajisi narrated to me, saying: Abul Qasim al-Baghowi narrated to us, saying: Ali (that is, ibn al-Ja'd) narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: Al-Walid ibn Al-izar ibn Hareeth narrated to me, saying: I heard Abu Amr al-Shaybani say: The owner of this house, pointing with his hand to the house of Abdullah ibn Mas'ood, said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family):

"What deeds are most beloved to Allah, the Exalted?" He said: "Prayer at its proper time." I said: "Then what?" He said: "Kindness to parents." I said: "Then what?" He said: "Jihad in the cause of Allah, the Exalted." He said: "He told me this, and if I had asked him for more, he would have given me more."
ai.seo_question: What are the three most beloved deeds to God according to the Prophet Muhammad?
ai.summary: Reported by Abdullah ibn Mas'ood in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Khisal*, this hadith establishes a spiritual hierarchy where punctual prayer (*Salat li-waqtiha*) takes precedence, followed by filial piety (*Birr al-Walidayn*) and striving in God's cause (*Jihad*). This ordering underscores the Shia emphasis on the foundational role of ritual worship and family bonds as the primary means of attaining divine pleasure, with *Jihad* serving as the subsequent act of devotion.
